messages:
Priya Nadar: heads-up — i'm about to open a draft PR to split the existing `network` module into `network-core` + `network-gke` in infra/. will push in ~10m. main things i want quick eyes on: provider pinning approach, lockfile churn, and the k8s secret path wiring for the gke module. can folks do a quick qa?

Alex Chen: thanks — can you paste the minimal module snippet you're planning to use and confirm terraform version + backend? also any state move plan?

Priya Nadar: sure, minimal example i'm going to include in the gke module:

```hcl
module "network-gke" {
  source = "../modules/network-gke"

  required_providers {
    google = {
      source  = "hashicorp/google"
      version = "~> 4.50"
    }
  }

  # inputs...
}
```

TF version: 1.5.x in CI (we're pinning to 1.5.9). backend: existing s3 backend (unchanged). plan for state: I want minimal state move (if any) — ideally we keep resource addresses the same but modules split might require `terraform state mv` in a controlled window.

Miguel Alvarez: quick notes:
- Modules should declare required_providers (good). matching the root pins is helpful but modules having the block avoids implicit provider resolution changes.
- Before merging: run a staged `terraform init` + `terraform plan` in a throwaway workspace so we can see provider address and resource addresses diffs.
- Lockfile: generate in the staging workspace so we can inspect the tf.lock.hcl diff. big churn usually comes from platform/platforms field or provider constraints.

Jordan Lee: +1 on doing a staged plan. also watch for the k8s secret path change — the gke module reads a secret path input and we changed default namespace interpolation last quarter. if the new module hardcodes namespace it could break existing clusters. please add a note in the PR about testing secret mounts.

Priya Nadar: good call. i'll add a `secret_path` input and preserve interpolation unless explicitly overridden. planning to include migration notes and an explicit `state move` section in the PR description if `terraform plan` shows address diffs.

Alex Chen: procedural suggestion:
1) open draft PR with module split + module versions + `tf.lock.hcl` regen in a new branch
2) create a staging workspace (`infra-net-split-staging`) that uses the same backend but a different workspace name
3) run `TF_WORKSPACE=infra-net-split-staging terraform init` then `terraform plan -out=split.plan` and attach the plan to the PR
4) if plan looks like only moves, prepare a small runbook with `terraform state mv` commands and test them in the staging workspace

Priya Nadar: copying your checklist. i'll do steps 1-3 and tag reviewers.

infra-bot: deploybot: created workspace `infra-net-split-staging` (queued), see https://ci.redwood.internal/org/infra/workspaces/infra-net-split-staging/plans/42 for the plan once it's ready.

Miguel Alvarez: tiny nit — in the modules, avoid pinning to an exact patch like `= 4.50.0` unless you want to control every patch. prefer a bounded range `~> 4.50` or `>= 4.50, <5.0` so minor provider fixes flow.

Priya Nadar: noted — i'll use `~> 4.50` in modules and include the root's `required_providers` with a range too.

Jordan Lee: i'll volunteer to run the state move rehearsals in the staging workspace once you have a plan attached. ping me in the PR and i can run the commands and report back.

Alex Chen: i'll take the code review after the plan is attached. one more check: make sure the CI runs the `make tf-validate` and `make tf-lint` for the new module paths.

Priya Nadar: thanks all — opening PR now. tagging @Alex Chen @Jordan Lee @Miguel Alvarez for review. will include explicit testing steps and how to validate the lockfile diffs. :thumbsup:

Miguel Alvarez: :eyes: will review plan output when CI posts it.

Alex Chen: :shipit: once the plan and state-move runbook look safe.

infra-bot: deploybot: plan complete and uploaded to PR (plan id 84).

Priya Nadar: uploaded the plan and the PR description includes `state-move` section + commands. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/3122 (draft).
